prompt: Why does the events app keep its templates in events/templates/events/ rather than events/templates/?

choices.text: So events/event_list.html cannot collide with another app's file
choices.why: Right. Django takes the first match across all apps.

choices.text: APP_DIRS requires two levels of directories
choices.why: It requires templates/; the second level is a convention for names.

choices.text: The admin reads templates only from that path
choices.why: The admin has its own templates.

choices.text: Without it, the templates would also be served as static files
choices.why: Templates are never served as files.

prompt: Match each piece of template syntax to what it is.

pairs.right: a link built from a pattern's name

prompt: The same template prints {{ event.title }} for a dictionary now and for a model object in lesson 4. Why does it work for both?

choices.text: Django converts every object to a dictionary before rendering
choices.why: No conversion happens.

choices.text: Models are dictionaries underneath
choices.why: They are classes with attributes.

choices.text: The dot tries a key, then an attribute
choices.why: Right, then a list index: one syntax, several kinds of lookup.

choices.text: Only because title is a reserved name in templates
choices.why: Any name works the same way.

prompt: The list printed Thu 12 Nov, 19:00 for Django Night. What decided that it was 19:00 and not 22:00?

choices.text: The date filter rounds to the venue's local time by guessing
choices.why: Nothing is guessed.

choices.text: The TIME_ZONE setting
choices.why: Right: America/Sao_Paulo. The filter shows the value in the current zone.

choices.text: The browser converted it
choices.why: The server wrote the text; curl converted nothing.

choices.text: USE_TZ is False in agenda
choices.why: It is True; values are aware datetimes.

prompt: What does {% block content %}{% endblock %} in base.html declare?

choices.text: A part of the page that child templates may not change
choices.why: It is the opposite: a part children fill.

choices.text: An include of content.html
choices.why: That would be {% include %}.

choices.text: A hole a child fills
choices.why: Right: a named hole, with an empty default here.

choices.text: A cache region for the rendered HTML
choices.why: Blocks have nothing to do with caching.

prompt: A child template has {% load static %} on its first line and {% extends "base.html" %} on the second. What happens?

choices.text: TemplateSyntaxError: extends must be the first tag
choices.why: Right. Text and comments before it are allowed; another tag is not.

choices.text: It works, since load only affects this file
choices.why: load is a tag, and extends must be the first one.

choices.text: The load is ignored and a warning is logged
choices.why: It is an error, not a warning.

choices.text: The page renders without the base template and its header
choices.why: Nothing renders; the template fails to load.

prompt: A child template puts a paragraph between {% extends %} and its first {% block %}. What becomes of the paragraph?
hint: Where would it go in the parent's page?

choices.text: It appears at the top of the page
choices.why: The child has no page of its own; only blocks are used.

choices.text: Rendering fails with an error naming the line
choices.why: No error is raised.

choices.text: It is appended to the content block
choices.why: Text outside blocks is not moved into one.

choices.text: It is silently thrown away
choices.why: Right, which is worse than an error.

prompt: Inside a child's block, {{ block.___ }} prints the parent's version of that block.
hint: A word for the parent class in Python.

prompt: The search term dojo came back in the page as <b>dojo</b>. What did that?

choices.text: The browser, when it sent the request
choices.why: curl sent it as typed; the server changed it.

choices.text: Django's automatic escaping of {{ q }}
choices.why: Right. Every variable is escaped unless told otherwise.

choices.text: A filter in the view that removes tags
choices.why: The view passes q unchanged.

choices.text: CsrfViewMiddleware, which cleans query strings
choices.why: It only checks POSTs.

prompt: Which is the defence against cross-site scripting that the lesson recommends?
hint: Where does the defence happen: on the way in or on the way out?

choices.text: Filtering dangerous words like script out of every form field
choices.why: Filters always miss a case.

choices.text: Marking trusted variables with |safe
choices.why: |safe turns protection off.

choices.text: Escaping on output, everywhere
choices.why: Right, which the template does by default.

choices.text: Refusing requests whose URL has < in it
choices.why: Legitimate text contains <, and escaping handles it.

prompt: Which of these may reasonably go through |safe? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: HTML produced by a Markdown renderer the application trusts
choices.why: Right. The application made it.

choices.text: The name a person typed into the registration form
choices.why: Never: that is the defect itself.

choices.text: A fragment built by your own code with every variable escaped
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The search term from the query string
choices.why: It came from whoever wrote the link.

prompt: A POST to the detail page without csrfmiddlewaretoken answered 403. What would make the same POST pass?

choices.text: Sending it twice
choices.why: Repeating changes nothing.

choices.text: Adding a Referer header
choices.why: Over plain HTTP the cookie and the token are what is checked.

choices.text: The csrftoken cookie and a matching token field
choices.why: Right, as curl did with cookies.txt.

choices.text: Logging in first
choices.why: CSRF is checked whether or not anybody is logged in.

prompt: Why can a page on another site not forge agenda's registration POST, even though the browser attaches agenda's cookies?
hint: What does the attacker's page lack?

choices.text: It cannot read agenda's HTML to learn the token
choices.why: Right. The cookie goes along; the token does not.

choices.text: Browsers refuse to post forms to another site
choices.why: They allow it, which is why CSRF exists.

choices.text: agenda checks the visitor's IP address
choices.why: It checks nothing of the kind.

choices.text: The cookie expires when the person opens another site in a tab
choices.why: Cookies do not expire that way.

prompt: Put a successful registration in order, as the lesson's figure draws it.
items: GET the page: form, token, csrftoken cookie
POST the form with the cookie and the token
GET the page again: 1 of 12 seats taken
trap: Rendering the page in answer to the POST, instead of redirecting, would make F5 register the person again.

prompt: The browser shows a required name field and checks the email type itself. Why does the server validate anyway?
hint: Who else can send a POST?

choices.text: Browsers validate only in development mode
choices.why: They validate always; that is not the reason.

choices.text: Django cannot read the browser's verdict
choices.why: There is no verdict sent; the point is who sends.

choices.text: Anything that skips the page, curl for one, sends whatever it likes
choices.why: Right. Browser checks are a convenience for the person.

choices.text: To translate the error messages
choices.why: Translation is not why validation runs twice.

prompt: Two people submit the last seat of the workshop at the same instant. With lesson 3's code, what can happen?

choices.text: Django queues the requests, so the second always sees the event full
choices.why: Nothing serialises the check and the append.

choices.text: Both see eleven taken and both are registered
choices.why: Right. Lesson 4 makes the database enforce the capacity.

choices.text: Both get This event is full
choices.why: Neither saw twelve.

choices.text: The CSRF check refuses the second, since its token was already used
choices.why: Tokens are not single-use; both are valid.

prompt: After Bruno and eleven more people registered, how many seats did the workshop page say were taken?
Why did runserver serve /static/events/agenda.css?

choices.text: DEBUG is on, so staticfiles serves it
choices.why: Right: staticfiles adds a handler to the development server. With DEBUG off nothing in Django serves it.

choices.text: Every Django view also serves files
choices.why: Views run code; they do not serve directories.

choices.text: The {% static %} tag uploaded it
choices.why: The tag only writes an address.

choices.text: collectstatic ran automatically at start-up
choices.why: Nobody ran collectstatic.

prompt: Match each piece to its job in serving static files in production.
hint: The table at the end of the section.

copies every app's static/ into it

prompt: Which of these template mistakes produces no error at all?
hint: One of them prints an empty string.

choices.text: {% for %} with no {% endfor %}
choices.why: TemplateSyntaxError: Unclosed tag.

choices.text: {{ event.titel }}
choices.why: Right. An unresolved variable prints nothing.

choices.text: {{ event.starts_at|dat }}
choices.why: TemplateSyntaxError: Invalid filter.

choices.text: render(request, 'events/event_lsit.html')
choices.why: TemplateDoesNotExist.

prompt: Why does Django print an empty string for a variable it cannot resolve, instead of failing?

choices.text: Templates cannot raise exceptions
choices.why: They raise several, as this section showed.

choices.text: It is a bug Django keeps for compatibility with old templates
choices.why: It is a deliberate choice.

choices.text: To hide the database from attackers
choices.why: The database has nothing to do with it.

choices.text: So a missing optional value does not take the page down
choices.why: Right, at the price of silent typos.

prompt: Which development-only setting makes misspelled variables visible on the page?
hint: It goes in the OPTIONS of TEMPLATES.

choices.text: DEBUG = True
choices.why: DEBUG was already on, and the typo printed nothing.

choices.text: string_if_invalid
choices.why: Right, with something like 'MISSING %s'.

choices.text: APP_DIRS = False
choices.why: That stops Django finding app templates.

choices.text: TEMPLATE_DEBUG = True
choices.why: That setting was removed long ago.

prompt: A colleague fixes a page that shows a blank where the event title should be by adding |default:'Untitled' to {{ event.titel }}. What is the problem?

choices.text: default does not accept strings
choices.why: It accepts any value.

choices.text: Filters cannot follow a dotted variable
choices.why: They can.

choices.text: The name is misspelled; every event will now say Untitled
choices.why: Right. The real fix is titel to title.

choices.text: Nothing; that is the recommended fix
choices.why: It hides the typo instead of fixing it.
